plain_text:
Research has shown the most effective strategy to increase booster seat
use is through updating, implementing, and enforcing state child restraint
laws $^{13}$ with booster seat provisions.
$^{14-18}$ These are commonly known as
“booster seat laws.
” In addition to increasing booster seat use, booster seat
laws also reduce motor vehicle-related injuries and deaths in children under
age 9 who are covered by these laws.
$^{14,15,19}$

plain_text:
Most state laws do not align with best practice recommendations despite
demonstrated effectiveness.
20 As of March 2024, only 5 states require
children to use booster seats until at least age 9: Hawaii, Louisiana,
Tennessee, Washington, and Wyoming.
20 Increasing the number of STLTs
with booster seat laws that cover children until at least age 9 will increase
booster seat use and help protect more children from a leading cause of
injury and death.
